answer: Cut-bounded trust propagation resists sybils: trust flows from a seeded honest core along attestation edges, and the total any region can receive is capped by the capacity of the edge-cut separating it from the core — not by how many identities or internal edges it holds. A sybil cluster hides behind a narrow lagoon of a few cross-edges; like a comet trailing one thin tail, the whole swarm shares that bottleneck. Add a walnut-shell army of fakes and aggregate trust stays bounded by the cut, since internal edges carry no flow across it. Honest agents sit on wide cuts and inherit full trust.
